Consent

By answering the following questions, you are participating in a study being performed by cognitive scientists in the Stanford Department of Psychology. If you have questions about this research, please contact us at stanfordpsych251@gmail.com. You must be at least 18 years old to participate. Your participation in this research is voluntary. You may decline to answer any or all of the following questions. You may decline further participation, at any time, without adverse consequences. Your anonymity is assured; the researchers who have requested your participation will not receive any personal information about you.

This part of the study uses sound. Please put on headphones or turn on your speakers.

Click Play test sound as many times as you like and set your volume to a comfortable level. Then click Continue.

Debrief

Thank you. This study tests whether people express emotions with the same patterns of speed, regularity, step size, direction and roughness in music and in movement. Some participants used the program to make melodies and others used the same sliders to make a bouncing ball move; we will compare the settings the two groups chose for each emotion. It replicates a study by Sievers and colleagues (2013). If you have questions about this research, contact stanfordpsych251@gmail.com. Press the button to save your responses and finish.
